extracted.intended_audience: ACL 2020 paper reviewers (NLP / computational linguistics conference reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers tasked with evaluating submissions to ACL 2020, covering how to fill the review form, scoring, confidentiality, use of supplementary material, secondary reviewers, and timelines. Focused on producing thorough, justified reviews for long and short papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of any submission to ACL2020, and the participants in and content of discussion on submissions, are confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share submission content or discussion outside the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the most important part. It should include your view of the main contributions that the paper intended to make and how well it succeeds at making these contributions. From your point of view, what are the significant strong and weak parts of the paper and the work it describes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a 2-paragraph (or longer) essay and/or a bullet list. Remember to describe how the work advances the state of knowledge in computational linguistics and/or why it fails to make a sufficient contribution. Provide evidence to support your opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to accept
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize from your core review the main reasons why this paper should be accepted for the conference, and how the ACL community would benefit from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may refer back to your core review for context and details; be concise but specific about community benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the possible risks or harm that might come from having this paper published and presented in something close to its current form. What are the parts that would need to be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify concrete weaknesses and required improvements that prevent the paper from advancing the state of knowledge in its current form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Synthesize the above and come up with your own recommendation for the paper using a 5-point scale with half-point increments. (The ambivalent rating 3 has been removed.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align your numeric recommendation with the reasoning provided in the core review. Decisions consider the whole review, discussion, and Area Chair meta-reviews, but reviewers should make a clear, justified recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL 2020 uses a 5 point scale with half point increments; rating 3 (ambivalent) has been removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the scale to express your overall opinion and the relative importance of factors; because rating 3 is removed, take a stand above or below the borderline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate how confident you are about your recommendation, taking into account your own expertise and familiarity with this area and the paper’s contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informs the committee and authors about how much weight to give your recommendation given your expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL 2020 will have an author response period. Check whether author responses have cleared up your questions or misunderstandings; this may influence your overall recommendation and the core review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the author response changes your view, update your recommendation and review accordingly and state any new decisions you made so Area Chairs are aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and additional feedback for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Place for questions you would like the author(s) to respond to during the response period and for suggestions to help authors improve the paper for the final version or a future submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to solicit clarifications and provide constructive, actionable feedback distinct from the confidential comments to chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information (to ACs/PC chairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Answers in this section are not shared with authors; includes recommended presentation type (oral vs. poster), award recommendations, ethical concerns, and confidential comments to area chairs and/or PC chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for matters you don't want communicated to authors but that are important for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: General guideline — balanced approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Take a balanced approach: seek a solid technical program with high-quality, complete work while keeping an open mind to a broad and interesting program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh completeness and rigor against novelty and interest; avoid being overly narrow about what counts as valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short paper guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A short paper is not a shortened long paper. Instead short papers should have a point that can be made in a few pages and present a focused contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate short papers on whether they present a clear, focused contribution appropriate to the shorter format rather than expecting full long-paper scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary materials are allowed as a stand-alone document uploaded as an additional file. They are supplementary and you have no obligation to read them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat supplementary materials like other citations — potentially helpful for background or details beyond the paper's scope, but reviewers are not required to consult them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary reviewers policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You are allowed to solicit help from others. However, when writing the final review and giving final scores, you must take the secondary reviewer’s review, rewrite it using your own words and adjust the scores when you see fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final review should reflect your own opinions about the paper and you must be able to justify the opinions and scores you present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Program chairs and area chairs have identified and desk-rejected submissions that violated formatting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers do not need to worry about formatting issues for submissions assigned to them, as format-violating papers have been handled already.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers were assigned no more than 6 reviews each; since there was a joint long and short paper deadline you may have a combination of long and short papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are due by the stated deadline (midnight anywhere on Earth). There is a reviewer discussion period after the author response; do not leave reviewing to the last minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision context and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions are made not just on scores but take into account the whole review, reviewer discussion, and Area Chair meta-reviews and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nevertheless, align your recommendation with the reasoning in your review so authors and chairs can understand the motivation for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult external reviewing advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are encouraged to consult excellent advice from experienced reviewers and conference organizers (linked blog posts and sample reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended external resources include ACL/NAACL blog posts and sample reviews highlighting mistakes to avoid and examples of good reviews.
